## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). 3-bets/4-bets extremely wide — including premiums (AA). **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything — including calling multi-street donk-leads with just overcards. C-bets most flops, checks dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); MEDIUM HANDS → checks turn, calls river (station mode); REAL HANDS → shoves aggressively. Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **As NON-PFA (BB defend, etc.)**: Fit-or-fold — folds to c-bets when whiffing. Stabs turn with marginal holdings but gives up river on scary boards. **DONK-LEADS with strong made hands (especially in 3-bet pots).** **CHECK-RAISES with semi-bluffs/draws on wet boards** — barrels turn with equity, CHECK-FOLDS river when draw misses. **Key line: P2 check-raise flop → bet turn → check river = BUSTED DRAW — attack with river bet.** Calls 3-bets with pocket pairs (including JJ). **Exploit**: Flat opens IP with suited broadways/connectors. 3-bet QQ+/AKs only. Value bet extremely thin as PFA. Float flop c-bets. DO NOT bluff when P2 is calling with made hands. DO bluff when P2's line = busted draw. As 3-bet caller: c-bet when P2 checks (will fold air); FOLD to P2's donk-lead + turn aggression (strong). **P2 bleeds chips every session — finished near-busted ($305) in S3. Primary value target. 3 sessions of confirmed losing.**

**Player 3**: **Tight-aggressive, skilled — but consistently loses.** Went BUST in S3 ($0). Completes SB wide (including QJo), then plays aggressively postflop. 3-bets from blinds vs ALL positions. **Confirmed trapper — wide check-raise range in BOTH 3-bet pots AND limped pots.** Will CHECK-RAISE ALL-IN with as little as top pair in limped pots. C-betting is SELECTIVE. Triple-barrels one-pair value. **Vs RAISED POTS with escalating pressure**: calls flop+turn then folds river to size. **Vs LIMPED/SMALL POTS: stickier AND more aggressive — check-raises with top pair, calls down light.** **Exploit**: Multi-street barrels work in raised pots. In limped pots, don't bluff into P3 — they fight back. Value bet wider in limped pots. Good steal target in blinds. **If P3 rebuys, may be tilted or adjusting after bust-out — monitor early for changes.**

**Player 4**: **Loose-passive preflop, WILDLY UNPREDICTABLE postflop — part station, part maniac. THE most consistent accumulator across 3 sessions (always finishes top 2-3).** Calls wide preflop (3-bets with junk, limps wide). **CRITICAL: Capable of MASSIVE bluffs — confirmed shoved all-in with complete air (7-high, no draw) on paired board in limped pot.** Also bets multiway flops with marginal holdings. As LIMPER: Will bet flop AND shove turn with ZERO equity. ALSO still a calling station — calls river with bottom pair, 9-high. **Dual nature: bluffs huge AND calls down light.** PASSIVE with strong made hands — checks made straights through all streets. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+) but folds to 4-bets. 5-BET SHOVE includes JJ.** As single-raiser: C-bets flop, folds to turn raises — FLOATABLE. **Folds SB to button steals with sub-premium hands — confirmed.** **Exploit**: Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target when calling). DON'T auto-fold to P4's aggression in limped pots — can be pure air. CALL DOWN wider vs P4 aggression (especially limped pots). In raised pots as PFA, still floatable. Steal over P4's SB freely. **P4 is the hardest opponent to read — respect their stack, exploit their wide calling.**

**Player 5**: **Tight nit (~7% VPIP) but EFFECTIVE chip accumulator — finished well all 3 sessions.** Even when SHORT-STACKED, 3-bet/shove range remains premium-heavy (confirmed AA at ~5.5BB). Limps with pocket pairs, stabs flop with small bets. C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. **As CALLER facing aggression: will call ONE street then FOLDS to continued betting, especially with scare cards.** Donk-bets can be strong OR weak — weak ones fold to raises/turn barrels; strong ones ESCALATE. **ANY turn raise from P5 = monster.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Multi-street value bet gets only 1-2 streets max — size up earlier streets for value. FOLD to P5's turn raises always. Good steal target in blinds. **BEWARE: P5's 3-bets are ALWAYS strong regardless of stack depth — give extra respect.**

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy — wide limper, opener, AND cold-caller. Roughly breaks even through volume.** **As LIMPER: EXTREMELY sticky postflop — calls with bottom pair. Folds preflop to large raises/steals.** **As COLD-CALLER: Donk-leads with AIR/weak draws → RAISE for fold equity. CHECK-CALLS with real made hands — passive line = actual hand.** Key tell: P6 donk-lead = air; P6 check-call = real hand. **P6 RAISES/RE-RAISES can be SEMI-BLUFFS with combo draws.** MASSIVE overbets = value. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED.** **Confirmed folds BB AND SB to button steals.** **Exploit**: Value bet wide. SIZE DOWN iso-raises (~3x) to keep P6 in when you have value. NEVER bluff check-calling P6. RAISE donk-leads (they're air). FOLD to 4-bet shoves/overbets. Steal over P6's blinds freely.

**Player 7**: **CONFIRMED extremely wide opener — opens trash hands (T3o from MP).** Wide limper too. **PREFLOP MANIAC in escalated pots** — limp-3bets with suited broadways (KQs confirmed), calls 5-bets with QQ/suited junk, 6-bets with weak aces. **Limp-raise range is VERY wide: any Ax, pocket pairs, AND suited broadways.** **Postflop**: Commits with made hands (two pair+) — will 3-bet flop and call off. **Exploit**: Iso-raise wide over P7's opens/limps — HIGHLY +EV. Value bet relentlessly. In reraised pots, get it in with any premium. **P7 consistently finishes last/near-last across all 3 sessions — primary dead money source.**

## Self-Assessment & Table Image

**IMAGE: DOMINANT — 3 consecutive 1st place finishes.** Opponents folding at extremely high rates. 71% of S3 wins were uncontested. Image is an asset but may trigger adjustments from better opponents (P4, P5).
- **FOLD EQUITY IS PRIMARY PROFIT DRIVER** — consistently 70%+ of wins are uncontested across all sessions.
- **VALIDATED STRATEGY**: ~40% VPIP with selective aggression. Printing money across 3 sessions.
- **PERSISTENT LEAK: Enter-then-fold.** Cost ~$300 in S3 (22 for -$200, two small losses at -$50 each). STILL the main improvement area. Ask: "Do I have a plan if raised?" before entering.
- **IMPROVEMENT FROM S2**: No late-session collapse. Won two biggest pots (hands 17-18) late. Discipline held.
- **TRACK RECORD**: S1: +$1665, 1st. S2: +$1510, 1st. S3: +$1200, 1st. Slight downward trend in profits — could be variance OR opponents slowly adjusting. Monitor.
- **ADJUSTMENT WATCH**: With 3 sessions of dominance, stronger opponents (P4, P5) may start playing back. Be ready to tighten slightly if 3-bet frequency against me increases.

## Core Strategy

1. **STEALING IS THE #1 EDGE** — continue opening wide from CO/BTN. P4 SB, P5, P6 SB/BB confirmed folding.
2. **Light 3-bet P2, P6, P7 opens** — fold equity high with image. P7 opens are often trash.
3. **COMMIT OR DON'T ENTER**: If investing 10%+ of stack, have a plan for full hand. Stop the enter-then-fold leak. This is the #1 improvement priority.
4. **Thin value > bluffing** against stations (P2, P4, P6). Image supports bluffs vs P3/P5 only.
5. **CALL DOWN P4 wider** — their aggression in limped pots can be pure air.
6. **Counter P2**: Flat opens IP, exploit postflop tendencies. Float flops — they check/fold turn without hands.
7. **Float P2 and P5 on flops** — both shut down on turn without hands.
8. **Multi-street barrels work vs P3 in RAISED pots**. In LIMPED pots, don't bluff P3.
9. **Never bluff sticky P6 (check-calling). RAISE P6's donk-leads (they're air).**
10. **ISO-RAISE P7 aggressively** — their opens AND limps are extremely wide.
11. **SIZE DOWN iso-raises vs P6** (~3x) to keep them calling dominated.
12. **Vs P5: front-load value extraction** — they fold rivers. Size up flop/turn bets. **RESPECT ALL 3-bets from P5 — always premium.**
13. **POSITIONAL AWARENESS for iso-raises**: When P5 is behind with a reshove stack, tighten iso-raise range or use smaller sizing.
14. **IMAGE MANAGEMENT**: If opponents start playing back more, have premiums ready. Don't auto-barrel into resistance just because fold equity has been high historically.

**Threat hierarchy (3 sessions confirmed)**: P4 (unpredictable accumulator, always top 3) > P5 (quiet nit, consistently finishes well) > P3 (skilled TAG but goes bust — volatile) > P6 (station, roughly breaks even) > P2 (volume LAG, always bleeds) > P7 (dead money, always finishes last).

**PRIORITY S4**: Maintain volume stealing. Fix enter-then-fold leak (plan every hand before investing). Watch for opponent adjustments to my dominant image. Stay disciplined.

Against this specific loose-passive texture (P1, P5), AQ is a trap hand when played for stacks pre-flop or on wet boards. ## Opponent Profiles

### Player 1 – Disciplined TAG (Value-Leaning, Structured Aggression)
- Solid open ranges; capable of open/folding to 3-bets.
- 4-bet range tight and premium-heavy.
- Linear 3-bet structure with broadways and medium+ pairs.
- Donk leads skew top-pair+.
- Double barrels turns for value on dynamic boards.
- River aggression is strongly value-weighted.
- Comfortable applying pressure when checked to in bloated pots; do not assume passivity after preflop flats.

**Exploit:**
- Increase IP 3-bets.
- Apply pressure when his range is capped.
- Avoid light 5-bets and thin river hero calls.
- Give more respect to large multiway/bloated-pot bets without strong bluff incentives.

---

### Player 3 – Loose-Passive Recreational (Wide Stack-Off / Nonstandard Preflop Lines)
- Calls preflop all-ins extremely wide, including dominated and weak holdings.
- Loose hand selection; low fold equity versus shoves.
- Bluff-catches at reasonable sizing.
- Passive unless holding strength.
- Capable of nonstandard preflop sizing/continuance; weird small raises are not automatically premium-only.

**Exploit:**
- Value jam wider; drastically reduce bluff jams.
- Value bet thinner postflop.
- Do not rely on fold equity when he covers.
- Treat unusual small preflop aggression as wider/less defined than a standard reg range.

---

### Player 4 – Structured TAG (Strong Value Raises)
- Tight preflop discipline.
- Flop raises in single-raised pots are heavily value-weighted.
- 3-bets/4-bets skew premium.
- Will call short-stack shoves wider than expected when covering.

**Exploit:**
- Overfold to flop raises without strong equity.
- Avoid light postflop 3-bet bluffs.
- Value shove appropriately when shallow.

---

### Player 5 – Passive TAG / Protection-Oriented, Slowplay Capable
- Limp/calls include pocket pairs.
- Donk-leads with medium-strength hands and draws (merged sizing).
- Flop checks do not cap range; can slowplay strong hands.
- Small-to-medium turn leads are merged, not purely weak.
- River aggression is extremely value-heavy.
- When river checking after earlier aggression, range is often medium-strength and can fold to pressure.

**Exploit:**
- Don’t auto-attack flop checks.
- Be selective floating turn leads.
- Overfold to river bets.
- Apply pressure more often when he checks river after leading earlier streets.

---

### Player 6 – Loose-Passive but Capable of River Stabs
- Limp/calls wide.
- Calls preflop all-ins lighter than population when covering.
- Generally passive postflop, but capable of bluff-leading rivers on scare cards after passive lines.
- River leads are not purely value.
- Still willing to call down with medium strength in other spots.

**Exploit:**
- Do not auto-overfold to river leads, especially on scare cards.
- Use blocker/range interaction analysis more carefully.
- Stay value-heavy versus his calling tendencies.
- Avoid assuming passivity means no bluffs.

---

### Player 7 – Loose-Passive, Not Pure Fit-or-Fold
- Limp-heavy preflop.
- Small turn donk bets can be blocking bets with medium pairs, not just weak draws.
- Will bluff-catch river with medium-strength hands.
- River betting remains more value-heavy than bluff-heavy, but his calling range is wider than initially assumed.

**Exploit:**
- Continue isolating preflop.
- Reduce assumptions that small donks = weakness.
- Bluff rivers less when he shows earlier-street interest.
- Value bet confidently when ahead.

---

## Strategic Notes / Self-Improvement

- With effective stacks under roughly 8 BB, simplify to a push/fold-oriented strategy; avoid flatting opens with weak speculative or dominated hands because SPR becomes too low to realize equity.
- Short-stack preflop decisions should be driven more by jam/fold thresholds than by trying to navigate postflop with marginal hands.
- In shallow spots, avoid getting bogged down in exact pot reconstruction mid-hand; default to cleaner preflop heuristics and preserve decision clarity.
